references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.32(1): all deductions in a salary period other than under s.27(1)(a) (absence), (f) (advances, loans, overpayments) and (j) (co-operative society) may not exceed 50% of the salary payable for that period — CPF contributions (s.27(1)(h)) count; s.32(2): the last salary on termination or completion of the contract is outside the limit. The independent per-instalment quarter caps of s.31(3) and (5) apply even on final salary; an excessive instalment is left wholly outstanding. See MOM Allowable salary deductions and JKB v JKC [2026] SGECT 11 paras.18–22. EA s.2 salary excludes travelling allowance, expense reimbursements, benefits in kind, gratuity and retrenchment benefits. Catalogue codes in basis_exempt_codes carry those classifications; customer-specific codes must be classified in the sealed settings. Salary overpayment and unearned-benefit recovery are outside s.31 instalment caps (MOM Allowable salary deductions). EA s.31(2): recovery of an advance is spread over no more than 12 months; the first scheduled instalment, including settled history, anchors the limit. EA ss.29–30: damage recovery is a one-time deduction limited to a quarter of one month salary; accepted accommodation and approved amenities/services share a quarter of salary-period salary, no more than their supplied value. These independent limits also apply on final pay. s.32(1) excludes consented registered-co-operative payments from its aggregate half. The damage limit applies per incident; the separate APPROVED_DAMAGE_RECOVERY class requires the Commissioner permission as evidence for the s.29(1) exception. The aggregate s.32 limit still applies. EA s.31(1): actual disbursed_on is required for an advance. If it was paid before employment, recovery starts only with the first completed salary period; pre-employment TRAVEL_ADVANCE is never recoverable from salary.

rules.description: IRAS, Tax clearance for employees, "When There is Additional Income Payable to Your Employee" (read 2026-10-07): file an Additional/Amended Form IR21 to seek further tax clearance before releasing the additional income; do not report it in the next IR8A/AIS. A payment after clearance is a slip of a period after the exit, or a slip after an earlier one in the exit period (an off-cycle run after the final pay). Ceiling: one recorded clearance releases every later payment. https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/employers/tax-clearance-for-foreign-spr-employees-(ir21)/tax-clearance-for-employees

Landscape: Addendum to the Tripartite Cluster for Landscape Industry report on the PWM Bonus, 3 July 2019 (https://www.mom.gov.sg/-/media/mom/documents/employment-practices/pwm/addendum-to-tcl-report-progressive-wage-model-bonus---3-july-2019.pdf), an NParks Landscape Company Register condition: the same quantum and service. references.title: Income Tax Act 1947 s.67(1)(a): records kept 5 years from the year of assessment; IRAS, Record keeping requirements (read 2026-10-07): a financial year ending in 2022 (YA 2023) is kept till 31 Dec 2027. The exit falls in a financial year ending in the exit year or the next, so the latest keep-till is 31 December of the exit year + 6. Longer than Employment Act 1968 s.95 with the Employment (Employee and Salary Records) regulations (1 year after the employee leaves; MOM, Employment records). Personal Data Protection Act 2012 s.25 then requires ceasing to retain the personal data (anonymising it).

rules.when: ((terms.statutory_work_category != "NON_MANUAL" && terms.base_salary <= 4500.0) || (terms.statutory_work_category == "NON_MANUAL" && terms.base_salary <= 2600.0)) && hours_between(day.intervals, "00:00", "00:00") > 12.0

rules.description: MOM, Employing young persons and children (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/young-persons-and-children), read 2026-10-07, on the Employment (Children and Young Persons) Regulations made under Employment Act 1968 ss.70, 73 (child: under 15; young person: 15, s.67A). rules.when: (has(employee.date_of_birth) && employee.date_of_birth != null && employee.date_of_birth != "" && age_on(employee.date_of_birth, day.date) < 16) && terms.statutory_work_category in ["MANUAL_LABOUR", "MANUAL_LABOUR_SUPERVISOR"] && has(day.intervals) && max_work_hours_between_breaks(day.intervals, 30) > (age_on(employee.date_of_birth, day.date) < 15 ? 3.0 : 4.0)
rules.message: A child doing manual labour may not work more than 3 hours, a young person more than 4, without a 30-minute break.
rules.description: MOM, Employing young persons and children (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/young-persons-and-children), read 2026-10-07, on the Employment (Children and Young Persons) Regulations made under Employment Act 1968 ss.70, 73 (child: under 15; young person: 15, s.67A). The maximum accumulated worked hours resets only after a break of at least 30 minutes. Shorter gaps do not reset it; overlapping or duplicated recorded intervals are counted once. School hours remain separately relevant to the daily cap.

name: Rest-day work without who asked for it

rules.when: employment.classification != "NON_EA" && ((terms.statutory_work_category != "NON_MANUAL" && terms.base_salary <= 4500.0) || (terms.statutory_work_category == "NON_MANUAL" && terms.base_salary <= 2600.0)) && size(work.days.filter(d, d.day_type == "REST" && d.worked_hours > 0.0)) > 0 && !has(employee.facts.rest_day_work_requester)
rules.message: Rest-day work is recorded but not who asked for it (employee.facts.rest_day_work_requester): EA s.37 pays 1 or 2 days at the employer’s request, ½ or 1 at the employee’s. Record it and rebuild before paying.
rules.description: Employment Act 1968 s.37(2)–(3): the rest-day pay depends on who requested the work; the slip is held rather than paying nothing.

name: Rest-day work without normal daily hours

rules.when: employment.classification != "NON_EA" && ((terms.statutory_work_category != "NON_MANUAL" && terms.base_salary <= 4500.0) || (terms.statutory_work_category == "NON_MANUAL" && terms.base_salary <= 2600.0)) && size(work.days.filter(d, d.day_type == "REST" && d.worked_hours > 0.0)) > 0 && !((has(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours) ? double(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours) : size(work.days.filter(w, w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0)) > 0 ? double(first(work.days.filter(w, w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0).map(w, w.scheduled_hours))) : 0.0) > 0.0)
rules.message: Rest-day work is recorded but the normal daily hours are unknown (no employee.facts.normal_daily_hours and no planned working shift): EA s.37 pays by whether the work exceeded half of them. Record them and rebuild before paying.
rules.description: Employment Act 1968 s.37(2)–(3): half or more of the normal daily hours decides the rest-day pay; the slip is held rather than paying nothing.

name: Part-time holiday work without contracted weekly hours

rules.when: terms.employment_type == "PART_TIME" && !has(employee.facts.part_time_weekly_hours) && size(work.days.filter(d, has(d.holiday_kind) && d.holiday_kind in ["PUBLIC_HOLIDAY", "SUBSTITUTE"] && d.worked_hours > 0.0)) > 0
rules.message: A part-timer worked a public holiday but the contracted weekly hours (employee.facts.part_time_weekly_hours) are not recorded, so the hourly basic rate cannot be set. Record them and rebuild before paying.
rules.description: Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations: holiday work is paid at the hourly basic rate from the contracted hours; the slip is held rather than paying nothing.
